arxiv-2402-05915.title: Cosmic-ray induced ionization rates and non-thermal emissions from nuclei of starburst galaxies 2024 Cosmic-ray induced ionization rates and non-thermal emissions from nuclei of starburst galaxies – 5
arxiv-2402-05915.creator: Vo Hong Minh Phan, Enrico Peretti, Pierre Cristofari, Antoine Gusdorf, Philipp Mertsch
arxiv-2402-05915.description: Abstract Cosmic rays are the only agent capable of ionizing the interior of dense molecular clouds and, thus, they are believed to play an essential role in determining the physical and chemical evolution of star-forming regions. In this work, we aim to study cosmic-ray induced ionization rates in starburst environments using non-thermal emissions of cosmic rays from starburst nuclei.

arxiv-2507-13563.description: Abstract This work is still in progress Russian speech synthesis presents distinctive challenges, including vowel reduction, consonant devoicing, variable stress patterns, homograph ambiguity, and unnatural intonation. This paper introduces Balalaika, a novel dataset comprising more than 2,000 hours of studio-quality Russian speech with comprehensive textual annotations, including punctuation and stress markings.

arxiv-2602-14960.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Pranav Kasela, Marco Braga, Ophir Frieder, Nazli Goharian, Gabriella Pasi, Raffaele Perego. Neural models are increasingly used in Web-scale Information Retrieval (IR). However, relying on these models introduces substantial computational and energy requirements, leading to increasing attention toward their environmental cost and the sustainability of large-scale deployments. While neural IR models deliver high retrieval effectiveness, their scalability is constrained in multi-domain scenarios, where training and maintaining domain-specific models is inefficient and achieving robust cross-domain generalisation within a unified model remains difficult.

pmc-13355378.description: Highlights•Galactose-metabolic (GM) reprogramming is the top dysregulated pathway in KRAS-mutant LUAD and correlates with “cold” immune microenvironment.•Single-cell and bulk multi-omics reveal two GM-based subtypes: high-GM/C1 (poor survival, KEAP1 co-mutations) vs low-GM/C2 (high TMB, robust CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration).•101-algorithm machine-learning screen establishes a 37-gene GM signature whose risk score outperforms clinicopathologic factors for predicting overall survival.
